mainTopic: Taanit 18a: The days next to the holidays of מגילת תענית. Why ראש חודש ניסן and the 8th of ניסן are listed, and the rulings of רב, שמואל and רבי יוחנן on רבי יוסי's view.
overview: This amud deals with the holidays listed in מגילת תענית and the days next to them. It opens at the end of an answer: some dates are listed only so that the day next to them is also forbidden. That follows רבי יוסי, who forbids both the day before and the day after a listed date. The גמרא then asks why ראש חודש ניסן is needed to forbid the 29th of אדר. The 29th already comes right after the 28th of אדר, a holiday from the time a Roman decree was cancelled, as a ברייתא tells. אביי answers that the listing matters when אדר has 30 days. רב אשי answers that a day between two holidays is treated like a holiday itself, so even הספד is forbidden on it. The גמרא adds that a separate listing protects a day in case another holiday is cancelled, which explains both the 8th of ניסן and the 29th of אדר. Then רב rules like רבי יוסי, while שמואל ends up following the most lenient view, that of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. רבי יוחנן's ruling like רבי יוסי is limited to the fasting days, and the גמרא begins challenging it from a סתם משנה about reading the מגילה early. That challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Listing the end of the holiday to forbid the day after
steps.stepSummary: Earlier, ראש חודש ניסן was explained as listed only to forbid the day before it. In the same way, the end of the פסח period is listed only to forbid the day after it.
steps.simpleTranslation: [Just as that listing was needed] only to forbid the day before it, here too it was needed only to forbid the day after it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes answering why מגילת תענית mentions a day that is already a holiday. It explains that the real purpose of the listing is to forbid eulogies on the neighboring day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This amud starts in the middle of a comparison. Before this, ראש חודש ניסן was explained as listed to forbid the day before it, the 29th of אדר. Now the same reasoning is used for the end of the פסח period: listing it adds a ban on the day after it.
steps.confusionAlert: This amud begins in the middle of a sentence. The words 'only to forbid the day before' belong to the earlier answer about ראש חודש ניסן. The new point is 'here too, to forbid the day after.'

phrases.english: only to prohibit the day before it,
phrases.notes: End of the earlier answer about ראש חודש ניסן.

phrases.english: here too —
it was needed only
to prohibit the day after it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא נָמֵי לָא נִצְרְכָה אֶלָּא לֶאֱסוֹר יוֹם שֶׁלְּאַחֲרָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the earlier explanation (the day before ראש חודש) as a model for this case (the day after the holiday).
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the listing a new purpose: it forbids the neighboring day.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Listing a day that is already a holiday seems pointless.
steps.terutzMaskana: The listing extends the ban to the day after it.

steps.title: Whose opinion is this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא holds that the day after a listed date is also forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: In accordance with whom?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which Sage this explanation follows. This short question sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not every תנא agrees that the days next to a listed date are forbidden. So the גמרא needs to identify whose view supports the answer from Step 1.

phrases.english: In accordance with whom?

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַאן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the view used in Step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that the day after a listed date is also forbidden.

steps.title: It follows רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: The view follows רבי יוסי, who forbids eulogies both on the day before and on the day after a listed date.
steps.simpleTranslation: In accordance with רבי יוסי, who said: both before it and after it are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the explanation follows רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי says the ban spreads to both sides of a listed date. This rule is what makes the next question possible.

keyTerms.meaning: the תנא who forbids both neighboring days
both before it and after it

steps.whyThisMatters: Under רבי יוסי's rule, every holiday listed in מגילת תענית also forbids the days next to it. The next question is built on this.

phrases.english: In accordance with Rabbi Yosei, who said:
both before it and after it are prohibited.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי דְּאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from Step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The view is רבי יוסי's: both the day before and the day after a listed date are forbidden.

steps.title: The 29th of אדר is already forbidden for another reason
steps.stepSummary: If רבי יוסי is right, the 29th of אדר is already forbidden because it is the day after the 28th of אדר. So why list ראש חודש ניסן just to forbid the 29th?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, regarding the 29th too: why say it is forbidden specifically because it is the day before the day the תמיד was established? Derive it from the fact that it is the day after the 28th of the month!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the earlier explanation. It argues that the 29th of אדר does not need ראש חודש ניסן to make it forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ראש חודש ניסן was said to be listed only to forbid the day before it, the 29th of אדר. But the 28th of אדר is also a listed holiday. According to רבי יוסי, the day after it, the 29th, is already forbidden, so listing ראש חודש ניסן seems to add nothing.

phrases.english: If so,
regarding the twenty-ninth too —
why specifically because it is
the day before the day
on which the daily offering was established?
Derive it from the fact that it is
the day after the twenty-eighth of the month!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי בְּעֶשְׂרִים וְתִשְׁעָה נָמֵי מַאי אִירְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רבי יוסי's rule from Step 3 to challenge the explanation about ראש חודש ניסן.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that ראש חודש ניסן is listed only to forbid the 29th of אדר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The 29th is already forbidden as the day after the 28th of אדר holiday, so listing ראש חודש ניסן is unnecessary.

steps.title: Source that the 28th of אדר is a holiday
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that the 28th of אדר is a holiday: good news came that the Jews would not be stopped from learning Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: On the 28th of the month, good news came to the Jews that they would not be kept away from the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to prove that the 28th of אדר really is a listed holiday. This supports the challenge in Step 4.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question in Step 4 only works if the 28th of אדר is a holiday. The ברייתא quotes מגילת תענית to confirm that it is.

keyTerms.meaning: as it is taught in a ברייתא
they would be removed or kept away

phrases.english: As it is taught:
On the twenty-eighth of the month,
good tidings came to the Jews
that they would not be kept away from the Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא בְּעֶשְׂרִים וּתְמָנְיָא בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up the premise of the question in Step 4.
steps.raayaObject: That the 28th of אדר is a holiday listed in מגילת תענית.

steps.title: The Roman decree and the request for advice
steps.stepSummary: Rome decreed against Torah study, מילה, and שבת. יהודה בן שמוע and his colleagues went to ask advice from a Roman noblewoman who was close to the leaders of Rome.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once the wicked kingdom decreed persecution on Israel: that they may not learn Torah, may not circumcise their sons, and must break שבת. What did יהודה בן שמוע and his colleagues do? They went and took advice from a noblewoman whom all the great men of Rome visited.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא tells the background story of the 28th of אדר: a harsh decree, and the Sages looking for help.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story explains why the day became a holiday. The decree attacked three basics of Jewish life: Torah study, ברית מילה, and שבת. The Sages looked for someone with influence over Rome's rulers.

keyTerms.meaning: a student of רבי מאיר who led the effort

phrases.english: For once the wicked kingdom decreed
religious persecution upon Israel:
that they may not engage in Torah,
and that they may not circumcise their sons,
and that they must desecrate Shabbatot.

phrases.aramaic: מָה עָשָׂה יְהוּדָה בֶּן שַׁמּוּעַ וַחֲבֵרָיו?
phrases.english: What did Yehuda ben Shammua and his colleagues do?
They went and took advice
from a certain Roman noblewoman
whom all the great men of Rome frequented.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁפַּעַם אַחַת גָּזְרָה מַלְכוּת הָרְשָׁעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא with the story behind the holiday.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Narrative background: Rome issued a decree against Torah, מילה, and שבת, and the Sages sought advice.

steps.title: The night protest and the decree is cancelled
steps.stepSummary: Following the noblewoman's advice, the Sages cried out at night that all people are brothers. The decree was cancelled, and that day became a יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: She told them: Get up and cry out at night. They went and cried out at night, saying: O Heaven! Are we not brothers? Are we not children of one father? Are we not children of one mother? How are we different from every nation and language, that you decree evil decrees against us? And they cancelled them, and that day was made a יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes the story. The protest worked, and the day was set as a holiday.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ending confirms that the 28th of אדר is a יום טוב in מגילת תענית. That brings back the question from Step 4 at full strength: the 29th is already forbidden as the day after it.
steps.whatToRemember: The 28th of אדר is a holiday because the Roman decree was cancelled. Under רבי יוסי, the 29th is then forbidden as the day after it.

phrases.english: She said to them:
Arise and cry out at night.
They went and cried out at night,
saying: O Heaven!
Are we not brothers?
Are we not children of one father?
Are we not children of one mother?
How are we different from every nation and tongue,
that you decree evil decrees against us!
And they annulled them,
and that day they made a holiday.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרָה לָהֶם עִמְדוּ וְהַפְגִּינוּ בַּלַּיְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא's story and confirms the holiday.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The 28th of אדר is a יום טוב, so the question in Step 4 stands.
steps.raayaObject: That the 28th of אדר is a יום טוב listed in מגילת תענית, so under רבי יוסי the 29th is already forbidden as the day after it.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The end of the ברייתא (מגילת תענית): the decree was annulled and that day was made a יום טוב.

steps.title: אביי: listing ראש חודש ניסן is needed for a 30-day אדר
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that listing ראש חודש ניסן matters when אדר has 30 days. Then the day before ראש חודש is the 30th, which is not right after the 28th.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It was needed only for a full (30-day) month.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question from Step 4. He explains when listing ראש חודש ניסן adds a ban that would not exist otherwise.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If אדר has 29 days, the day before ראש חודש is the 29th, which is already forbidden as the day after the 28th. But if אדר has 30 days, the day before ראש חודש is the 30th. The 28th does not reach the 30th, so only the ראש חודש ניסן listing forbids it.

keyTerms.meaning: the אמורא who gives the answer

steps.whatToRemember: Listing ראש חודש ניסן is not extra. In a 30-day אדר it forbids the 30th of אדר, which the 28th of אדר holiday does not cover.
steps.confusionAlert: Here חֹדֶשׁ מְעוּבָּר means a 30-day month, not a leap year with an extra אדר.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
It is necessary only for a full (thirty-day) month.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי לֹא נִצְרְכָה אֶלָּא לְחֹדֶשׁ מְעוּבָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from Step 4, which the ברייתא strengthened.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrows the case: the listing matters in a specific calendar situation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Listing ראש חודש ניסן seems unnecessary, since the 29th is already forbidden because of the 28th.
steps.terutzMaskana: In a 30-day אדר, the 30th is forbidden only because of the ראש חודש ניסן listing.

steps.title: רב אשי: A day between two holidays is treated like a holiday itself
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says that even in a 29-day אדר, listing ראש חודש ניסן adds something. A plain 'day after' a holiday forbids only fasting. A day squeezed between two holidays forbids even הספד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Even if you say we are talking about a short month of 29 days, the listing still matters. Every day that comes after a listed holiday forbids fasting but permits eulogizing. But this day, the 29th of אדר, sits between two holidays: the 28th of אדר and ראש חודש ניסן. So the Sages made it like a holiday itself, and even eulogizing is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a second answer to the question from Step 4. He shows that listing ראש חודש ניסן makes the 29th of אדר stricter, even when אדר has only 29 days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי only solved the case of a 30-day אדר. רב אשי solves the 29-day case too. Being 'the day after' a holiday forbids only a תענית. Being 'between two holidays' raises the 29th to full holiday status, so הספד is also forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: The day that comes after it
A eulogy; mourning speech for the dead

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think 'the day after a holiday' and 'the holiday itself' have the same rules. The day after forbids only fasting. A real holiday, or a day squeezed between two holidays, forbids even הספד.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a day's status in מגילת תענית can be upgraded by its position in the calendar. Being sandwiched between two holidays gives it more than just 'day after' status.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Even if you say it refers to a deficient (29-day) month,
for every day that comes after a listed day —
phrases.notes: The 'day after' each holiday in מגילת תענית

phrases.english: fasting is forbidden, but eulogizing is permitted.

phrases.aramaic: וְזֶה, הוֹאִיל וּמוּטָל בֵּין שְׁנֵי יָמִים טוֹבִים —
phrases.english: But this day, since it is placed between two holidays —
phrases.notes: The 29th of אדר, between the 28th of אדר and ראש חודש ניסן

phrases.english: they made it like a holiday itself,
and even eulogizing is also forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא לְחוֹדֶשׁ חָסֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, different answer to the קשיא of Step 4. It also covers the 29-day month, which אביי's answer did not cover.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing levels of prohibition (fasting only vs. fasting and eulogy)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Listing ראש חודש ניסן seemed useless in a 29-day אדר, because the 29th is already forbidden as the day after the 28th.
steps.terutzMaskana: The listing upgrades the 29th from 'day after' (no fasting) to 'between two holidays' (no fasting and no eulogy).

steps.title: Quoting מגילת תענית: From the 8th of ניסן, the שבועות holiday was restored
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a line from מגילת תענית: from the 8th of ניסן until the end of פסח, a holiday was set to celebrate restoring the correct date of שבועות, and eulogizing is forbidden. This sets up the next question.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said (in מגילת תענית): From the 8th of ניסן until the end of the festival (פסח), the festival of שבועות was restored, and so one may not eulogize.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line from מגילת תענית. This is a setup line, and the גמרא is about to ask a question about its wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, מגילת תענית said that from ראש חודש ניסן until the 8th, the תמיד was established. This new line starts its own celebration on the 8th itself. The overlap on the 8th is what the next step will question.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Master said', a formula for re-quoting a source mentioned earlier

phrases.english: The Master said:
From the eighth of it (ניסן) until the end of the festival
the festival of Shavuot was restored,
phrases.notes: The correct calculation of שבועות was restored

phrases.english: so that one should not eulogize.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: מִתְּמָנְיָא בֵּיהּ וְעַד סוֹף מוֹעֲדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new line of מגילת תענית that raises a problem similar to the one just solved.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From the 8th of ניסן until the end of פסח, eulogizing is forbidden because the correct שבועות was restored.

steps.title: Why start from the 8th if the 8th is already forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the line starts from the 8th. The 8th is already forbidden as the last day of the תמיד celebration, so the line could have started from the 9th.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need it to say 'from the 8th'? Let it say 'from the 9th', and the 8th itself would already be forbidden, since it is a day on which the תמיד (daily offering) was established!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of the line just quoted. The 8th already seems covered by the תמיד celebration, so mentioning it again looks extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same kind of question as Step 4: why list a day that is already forbidden for another reason? The תמיד celebration runs from ראש חודש until the 8th, so the 8th is already a holiday. Starting the שבועות celebration on the 8th seems pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it? (asks why a detail is included)
The תמיד, the daily communal offering

phrases.english: Why do I need it to say 'from the eighth of it'?
Let it say 'from the ninth of it',
and the eighth itself is forbidden anyway,

phrases.aramaic: דְּהָוֵה לֵיהּ יוֹמָא דְּאִיתּוֹקַם בֵּיהּ תְּמִידָא!
phrases.english: since it is a day on which the daily offering was established!
phrases.notes: The 8th is the last day of the ראש חודש to 8th תמיד celebration

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמָה לִי לְמֵימַר מִתְּמָנְיָא בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the source quoted in Step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'from the eighth' in מגילת תענית
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Redundancy: the 8th is already forbidden as a תמיד-celebration day, so it did not need to be included again.

steps.title: In case the first celebration is cancelled, the 8th stands on its own
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that if something happened and the seven days of the תמיד celebration were cancelled, the 8th would still be forbidden. This is because it is the first day of the שבועות celebration.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since, if some event happened and they cancelled the seven days (of the תמיד celebration), the 8th itself would still be forbidden, because it is the first day on which the festival of שבועות was restored.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by imagining that the earlier holiday gets cancelled. Listing the 8th as part of the שבועות celebration protects it as a holiday no matter what.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Holidays in מגילת תענית could be cancelled if a disaster struck. If the תמיד days were cancelled, the 8th would lose that reason. Because the 8th is also the first day of the שבועות celebration, it keeps its holiday status independently.

keyTerms.meaning: Since, if it were to happen that

steps.confusionAlert: The seven cancelled days are the first seven days of the תמיד celebration. The 8th is the overlap day, and it survives because it belongs to the שבועות celebration too.

phrases.english: Since, if some event were to happen
and they cancelled the seven days —
phrases.notes: The seven days of the תמיד celebration

phrases.english: the eighth itself would still be forbidden,
since it is the first day
on which the festival of Shavuot was restored.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דְּאִילּוּ מִקְּלַע לֵיהּ מִילְּתָא וּבַטְּלִינֵּיהּ לְשִׁבְעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Backup reason (protection in case the first reason is cancelled)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Mentioning the 8th is extra, since the תמיד celebration already covers it.
steps.terutzMaskana: Mentioning the 8th gives it its own independent holiday status, which survives even if the תמיד days are cancelled.

steps.title: Same logic applied back to the 29th of אדר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא applies the 'backup reason' logic to the 29th of אדר. If the 28th were cancelled, the 29th would still be forbidden as the day before ראש חודש ניסן, when the תמיד celebration begins.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that you have come to this idea, the 29th (of אדר) also: since, if some event happened and they cancelled the 28th, the 29th itself would still be forbidden, because it is the day before the day on which the תמיד was established.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes the answer from Step 12 and uses it to give another answer to the original question from Step 4. Listing ראש חודש ניסן protects the 29th of אדר even if the 28th is cancelled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 4, the 29th seemed already forbidden as the day after the 28th. But if the 28th were cancelled, the 29th would lose that reason. Because ראש חודש ניסן is listed, the 29th stays forbidden as the day before that holiday.

keyTerms.meaning: Now that you have come to this (idea)

steps.whatToRemember: The same method solves both questions: a day that seems forbidden twice over gets its own listing. That way it stays forbidden even if one of the holidays is cancelled. This protects the 8th of ניסן and the 29th of אדר.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a third explanation for why מגילת תענית lists ראש חודש ניסן. It also closes the loop on the question from Step 4.

phrases.english: Now that you have come to this,
the twenty-ninth (of Adar) also:
since, if some event were to happen
and they cancelled the twenty-eighth —
the twenty-ninth itself would still be forbidden,
since it is the day before
the day on which the daily offering was established.
phrases.notes: ראש חודש ניסן, the start of the תמיד celebration

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא דְּאָתֵית לְהָכִי, עֶשְׂרִים וְתִשְׁעָה נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the reasoning of Step 12 and applies it back to the earlier question about the 29th of אדר (Step 4).
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Listing ראש חודש ניסן ensures the 29th of אדר stays forbidden as the day before a holiday, even if the 28th of אדר is ever cancelled.

steps.title: רב and שמואל disagree about the ruling
steps.stepSummary: רב rules like רבי יוסי, and שמואל rules like רבי מאיר, about the days around the holidays of מגילת תענית.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: רב חייא בר אסי said in the name of רב, 'The הלכה follows רבי יוסי.' And שמואל said, 'The הלכה follows רבי מאיר.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a dispute between two אמוראים about which תנא we follow for the days next to the holidays of מגילת תענית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי מאיר holds that on a no-הספד holiday, the day before is forbidden but the day after is allowed. רבי יוסי is stricter and forbids both the day before and the day after. רב follows the stricter view, and שמואל follows the more lenient one.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated. This introduces a statement or dispute of אמוראים.
The practical law follows the opinion of this person.
The stricter תנא here. He forbids הספד both before and after the holiday.
The תנא of the unattributed משנה. He forbids the day before and allows the day after.
A eulogy for someone who has died.

steps.confusionAlert: The name רבי מאיר does not appear in the משנה. The anonymous opinion in the משנה is understood to be his.

phrases.aramaic: אִיתְּמַר, רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אַסִּי אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: It was stated: Rav Chiyya bar Asi said in the name of Rav:
The law follows Rabbi Yosei,
phrases.notes: The day before and the day after are both forbidden.

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:
The law follows Rabbi Meir.
phrases.notes: The day before is forbidden, and the day after is allowed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר, רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אַסִּי אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from analyzing the dates in מגילת תענית to deciding the practical הלכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: the הלכה follows רבי יוסי. שמואל: the הלכה follows רבי מאיר.

steps.title: שמואל seems to contradict himself
steps.stepSummary: Elsewhere שמואל rules like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who allows both the day before and the day after. That does not match a ruling like רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did שמואל really say this? But a ברייתא teaches that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: Why does the text say 'on them' twice? To teach you that only the days themselves are forbidden, and the days before and after are allowed. And שמואל said, 'The הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges שמואל's ruling by pointing to a different ruling of his that does not fit with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל learns from the double word 'בהון' that only the holiday itself is restricted. So the day before and the day after are both allowed. If שמואל follows him, then he cannot also follow רבי מאיר, who forbids the day before.

keyTerms.meaning: Did he really say this? This is a formula that opens a contradiction.
But it was taught in a ברייתא.
Why does the text say this? It asks what the extra wording comes to teach.
On them. This word appears twice in מגילת תענית.
A תנא who holds the most lenient view here.

phrases.english: But did Shmuel really say this?
But it was taught in a baraita:
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
Why does the text say 'on them', 'on them', two times?
phrases.notes: The two phrases are 'not to eulogize on them' and 'not to fast on them'.

phrases.english: To tell you that they themselves are forbidden,
but the days before them and after them are allowed.
And Shmuel said:
The law follows Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל הָכִי? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks שמואל's ruling from Step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that the הלכה follows רבי מאיר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל elsewhere follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who allows the day before. רבי מאיר forbids the day before, so the two rulings conflict.

steps.title: שמואל changed his ruling to the more lenient view
steps.stepSummary: שמואל first ruled like רבי מאיר because he thought no one was more lenient. When he heard that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל was even more lenient, he switched.
steps.simpleTranslation: At first שמואל thought that since no תנא was as lenient as רבי מאיר, the הלכה follows רבי מאיר. Once he heard that רבן שמעון was even more lenient, he said the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction. The two rulings came at different times, and שמואל updated his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל had one consistent principle: follow the most lenient opinion in this matter. The two statements are not a real contradiction. His first ruling was given before he knew of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's view.

keyTerms.meaning: A sage of the period of the משנה.

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that an אמורא can change his ruling over time. It also shows that a ruling can be guided by a principle, here leniency, and not only by which תנא is quoted.

phrases.english: Originally he thought:
Since there is no tanna
who is as lenient as Rabbi Meir,
he said the law follows Rabbi Meir.
Once he heard that Rabban Shimon
is even more lenient,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל.
phrases.english: he said: The law follows Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵעִיקָּרָא סָבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in Step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Change of position over time. A retraction based on new information.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל's two rulings seem to contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל always followed the most lenient view he knew. His later ruling, like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, replaced the earlier one.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן also rules like רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: באלי reports, through רבי חייא בר אבא, that רבי יוחנן ruled like רבי יוסי, just as רב did.
steps.simpleTranslation: Similarly, באלי said in the name of רבי חייא בר אבא, in the name of רבי יוחנן: 'The הלכה follows רבי יוסי.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another אמורא, רבי יוחנן, who seems to agree with רב. This sets up the next step, where his ruling will be clarified.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'וכן' (similarly) links this to רב's ruling in Step 14. On the surface, it looks like רבי יוחנן follows רבי יוסי in everything.

keyTerms.meaning: And similarly. A matching opinion is being brought.
The name of a sage who passes on this report.
A leading אמורא of ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: And similarly, Bali said
that Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
The law follows Rabbi Yosei.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן אָמַר בָּאלִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רב's position and brings support for it from רבי יוחנן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן: the הלכה follows רבי יוסי.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's ruling applies only to fasting days
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא explains that רבי יוחנן followed רבי יוסי only for the 'no fasting' days, not for the 'no הספד' days.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא said to באלי: 'Let me explain it to you. When רבי יוחנן said the הלכה follows רבי יוסי, he meant only for the days marked "not to fast."'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא בר אבא narrows רבי יוחנן's ruling so that it covers only the fasting days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the 'no fasting' days, רבי יוסי forbids fasting on the day before, and רבי יוחנן agrees with that. For the 'no הספד' days, however, רבי יוחנן does not follow רבי יוסי's extra stringency. He holds that הספד on the day after is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Let me explain it to you.
'Not to fast.' The days in מגילת תענית on which fasting is forbidden.

steps.whatToRemember: רב follows רבי יוסי across the board. שמואל ends up following רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, the most lenient view. רבי יוחנן follows רבי יוסי only for the fasting days.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי יוחנן fully agrees with רב. The word 'וכן' made it look that way, but his ruling is limited to the fasting days.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya said to Bali:
I will explain it to you:
When Rabbi Yochanan said
the law follows Rabbi Yosei,
it was regarding the days marked 'not to fast'.
phrases.notes: It does not refer to the days marked 'not to eulogize'.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי חִיָּיא לְבָאלִי: אַסְבְּרַהּ לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the scope of רבי יוחנן's ruling from Step 17.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יוחנן follows רבי יוסי only for the fasting days, so fasting is forbidden on the day before. For the הספד days, he does not follow רבי יוסי's extra stringency.

steps.title: Did רבי יוחנן really rule like רבי יוסי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the report from Step 17-18. רבי יוחנן has a general rule that the הלכה follows an unattributed משנה, and that rule may clash with ruling like רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רבי יוחנן really say this? But רבי יוחנן said: the הלכה follows an unattributed משנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the report that רבי יוחנן ruled like רבי יוסי. It brings up רבי יוחנן's own famous rule as the basis for the challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן holds that whenever a משנה states a law without naming who said it (a סתם משנה), the הלכה follows it. If a סתם משנה disagrees with רבי יוסי, then רבי יוחנן could not have ruled like רבי יוסי. The גמרא now needs to show that such a משנה exists.

keyTerms.meaning: And did he really say...? (opens a challenge to a reported statement)
But didn't he say...? (brings a contradicting statement by the same person)
The הלכה follows an unattributed משנה
A משנה that states a law with no name attached

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a challenge from another אמורא. The גמרא sets רבי יוחנן against himself: his general rule (follow the סתם משנה) against his specific ruling (follow רבי יוסי).
steps.whyThisMatters: רבי יוחנן's rule 'הלכה כסתם משנה' is a basic tool for deciding הלכה across ש״ס. Here the גמרא uses it to test a specific ruling attributed to him.

phrases.english: And did Rabbi Yoḥanan really say this?
phrases.notes: Refers to the report in Steps 17-18 that he ruled like רבי יוסי.

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Yoḥanan say:
The halacha follows an unattributed mishna.
phrases.notes: His general principle for deciding law.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הָכִי? וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling attributed to רבי יוחנן in Steps 17-18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The report that רבי יוחנן ruled like רבי יוסי for the 'no fasting' days.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Contradiction between two statements of the same אמורא: he follows every סתם משנה, and a סתם משנה (about to be quoted) seems to disagree with רבי יוסי.

steps.title: Quoting the unattributed משנה about reading the מגילה early
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins quoting the סתם משנה it will use against רבי יוחנן's ruling. The משנה is about reading מגילת אסתר earlier than פורים. The quote continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we learned in a משנה: Even though they said that one may read the מגילה earlier but not later...
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא starts quoting the סתם משנה that will prove the challenge. The key part of the משנה comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some people, such as villagers, may read מגילת אסתר before the 14th of אדר but never after it. The משנה opens by stating this rule, and it will go on to say what is still allowed on those early reading days. That next part is what will clash with ruling like רבי יוסי.

keyTerms.meaning: And we learned in a משנה (introduces a quoted משנה)
We move it earlier (read the מגילה before the proper day)
We delay it (read the מגילה after the proper day)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not stop here thinking the proof is finished. 'Early but not late' is only the opening phrase. The actual point of the proof comes in the next words of the משנה.

phrases.english: And we learned in a mishna: Although they said,
phrases.notes: This is a סתם משנה (in מסכת מגילה), with no name attached.

phrases.english: one may read it earlier but not later,
phrases.notes: Refers to reading מגילת אסתר. The quote continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּתְנַן: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאָמְרוּ מַקְדִּימִין וְלֹא מְאַחֲרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the actual סתם משנה needed to complete the challenge raised in Step 19.
steps.raayaObject: The challenge that רבי יוחנן could not have ruled like רבי יוסי.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The סתם משנה in מסכת מגילה about reading the מגילה early (the quote continues on the next amud).
